policy_title: Accelerate Universal Credit Rollout and Combat Fraud
stated: The Conservative Party will accelerate the rollout of Universal Credit to all remaining legacy benefit claimants to ensure work always pays, and will clamp down on welfare fraud with a new Fraud Bill giving DWP powers similar to HMRC to identify, investigate, and pursue fraudsters.

source.quote: Accelerate the rollout of Universal Credit to ensure it always pays to work. We will move all of those remaining on outdated legacy benefits onto Universal Credit... Continue to clamp down on fraudsters. ...This will include a new Fraud Bill to give DWP powers similar to that of HMRC...

bearing_set.reason: UC migration from legacy benefits changes claimants' net incomes — some gain, some lose — directly affecting whether low-income households can afford essentials.
UC is explicitly designed to 'ensure work always pays' via taper rates and work allowances, materially affecting in-work income and employment incentives for low-paid workers.
Granting DWP HMRC-equivalent investigatory powers (data-matching, third-party financial access) raises genuine privacy and due-process concerns for benefit claimants subject to investigation.

The Fraud Bill grants DWP HMRC-style investigative and data-access powers over benefit claimants — a concrete expansion of state surveillance and coercive authority that bears directly on O10's privacy/freedom-from-state-coercion indicators.

Reducing welfare fraud (currently costing several billion pounds annually) through new enforcement powers is a direct fiscal mechanism that improves the funded/borrowed balance — a non-negligible O12 effect.

membership_note: Two distinct sub-policies: UC rollout bears on O4 (work incentives) and O2 (disposable income for transitioning claimants); the Fraud Bill bears on O10 (expanded DWP surveillance/coercive powers) and O12 (fraud savings improve fiscal position). O5 was considered for fraud-as-crime but the primary effect is fiscal rather than public safety, so it was excluded.
